transcript:
# TOWN OF SUTTON-ZONING BOARD OF APPEALS

## SUTTON TOWN HALL

## MEETING MINUTES

## September 3, 2026

Board Members in Attendance by Roll Call: C. Matera, present; D. Petrelli, present; R. Deschenes, present; Z. Foley, present

R. Deschenes read two (2) M.G. L. Ch39 §23.D affidavits into the record for himself and C. Matera as it pertained to M.G. L. Ch39 §23.D and the August 6, 2026 meeting allowing them to participate in the evening's proceedings.

### 7:00pm Public Hearing cont'd: 185 Worcester Providence Turnpike

**Applicant: Ian Hikel**

**Sp. Permit: Contractor's Yard for Plumbing Business**

D. Petrelli motioned to re-open the public hearing for 185 Worcester Providence Turnpike

2nd: Chris Matera

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye, D.Petrelli, Aye, R. Deschenes, aye, Z. Foley, Aye

Applicant was not present, though he had confirmed attendance.

For the purpose of allowing additional time for the applicant to arrive, C. Matera motioned to shuffle the order of hearings around and move the hearing to the end of the meeting.

2nd: D. Petrelli

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye; D.Petrelli, Aye; R. Deschenes, aye; Z. Foley, Aye

### 7:06pm. Public Hearing: 38 and 26R Oakhurst Road

**Dimensional Frontage Variance**

**Oakhurst Road LLC**

**Present: Raouf Mankaryous, Project Engineer / Alpha Omega Engineering**

**Chris Windle, Oakhurst Road LLC**

D. Petrelli motioned to re-open the hearing for Oakhurst Road LLC, 26R and 38 Oakhurst Road.

2nd: C. Matera

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye; D.Petrelli, Aye; R. Deschenes, Aye; Z. Foley, Aye

Motion passed

R. Mankaryous spoke on behalf of his client, C. Windle.

Route 146 (Worcester Providence Trnpke) was dedicated as a no access highway in 1950 and an ANR Plan endorsed by the Town's Planning Board in 1979 which approved frontage on Rte 146 as well as access from Oakhurst Road which was noted as another means access for that parcel. In 1981 it was noted that there was another layout plan calling out Rte 146 as a "limited" access highway with the property owners paying taxes for an assessed buildable lot until what was believed to be 1994. Records show that at that time the Assessor's Office labeled it as non-buildable. However, C. Windle was in receipt of an email from MA DOT stating that they never took away the frontage, but only took away the right to access through it. They tried to get an alternate access finding from the Planning Board who denied it stating that they lost the frontage according to "current" zoning. The applicant stated that the parcel was created prior to the current zoning. Because of the Planning Board's determination, their request from the ZBA was to allow a 53 foot strip of frontage they were purchasing be their new frontage. He added that in addition to the no access issue along Rte. 146 there were topography issues with a pond and stream. R. Mankaryous also noted that were new considerations for a variance which included the effect on town and public interest. It was noted that there would be an increase of taxes from $510.00 per year to up to $100,000.00 per year on land and added excise tax on vehicles once developed. It was added that there would be no negative effect on the town's school system. Mr. Windle would be extending the public water line about 800 feet up Oakhurst Road giving opportunity to others to connect to it. It was noted that the development of the land would be a benefit to both his client and would have no negative effect on the town itself.

L. Dahlin noted to the Board that frontage existed but access did not and one of the listed requirements for a variance was that the search for all other available options had to be exhausted first prior to coming to the Board. Due to the Planning Board's decision, the applicant could not move forward and was now faced with a "practical difficulty".

R. Deschenes agreed that it was a unique situation.

D. Petrelli questioned the applicant on what the planned project entailed.

C. Windle responded the zone was Office-Light Industrial and the use proposed would be consistent with the area zoning. He was proposing Industrial buildings to house contractors. He informed the Board that the Planning Board was not opposed to the project, and C. Matera finished his statement by saying "They just didn't want to decide on the issue".

R..Deschenes questioned how much of the parcel was developable as there were also power lines and wetlands and it was answered everything east of the power lines. It was a 20-acre parcel and they would be able to develop about 80 to 100,000 square feet of it. R. Deschenes noted it was good to know what percentage was usable on the site adding that they could not "jam a whole bunch of stuff in there".

C. Matera thought it would create a financial hardship for the applicant if the Board did not act on this. R. Deschenes agreed stating that the parcel becomes landlocked and this would be the only way to be able to use the property. R. Mankaryous added that there was another legal access which was a 12' cart path but it was not wide enough. The Board noted that the town would receive a benefit by the applicant bringing the water main up.

The Board agreed that it was a great project, and D. Petrelli added that the applicant just ran into a technicality which was "punted over to us".

Public Participation: None

D. Petrelli stated that the Planning Board would be involved moving forward so he did not see the need for a site visit.

Z. Foley noted that the applicant had done his due diligence therefore he had no questions. He reviewed the map and found nothing questionable and if not granted then the applicant was just paying taxes on a lot which nothing could be done with and he found that granting the request made the most sense.

D. Petrelli noted that the issue was not self-created and the parcel had a full history which resulted in a disqualification on "some sort of technicality like the definitions changing over time. He felt it was not their fault.

R. Deschenes read the definition of what was considered a practical difficulty related to zoning and noted that in this case they had the frontage, they just couldn't use it. The property owner proposes a reasonable use of the land which is being blocked by strict code adherence.

C.Matera motioned to approve the variance for 38 Oakhurst Road/26R Oakhurst Road

2nd: D. Petrelli

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye; D. Petrelli, Aye; R. Deschenes, Aye; Z. Foley, Aye

Motion passed

### Approval of Minutes

R. Deschenes asked the Board if there were any comments or corrections needed for the following sets of meeting minutes: February 12, 2026, March 5, 2026, April 2, 2026, April 30, 2026, July 9, 2026, and August 6, 2026. Hearing none, all sets of minutes were approved as read.

### Volunteer Action Form Applicant

Russell Longendorfer of 8 Alana Drive introduced himself to the Board and explained he had lived in Town for about 9 years with 3 children growing up here and with the intention to remain in town. He was looking at getting more involved with the Community.

R. Deschenes explained what the Board's functions were. D. Petrelli went over scheduling of meetings and site visits. Discussion ensued about the types of applications heard by the Board and the sections of MGL. that the Board adhered to. The applicant had questions about the role on the Board as an alternate.

D. Petrelli motioned to recommend Russell Longendorfer to the Select Board.

2nd:C. Matera

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye; D. Petrelli, Aye; R. Deschenes, Aye; Z. Foley, Aye

Motion passed

### 7:47pm 185 Worcester Prov. Trpke

D. Petrelli motioned to re-open Ian Hikel's application for 185 WPTKE

C. Matera counter motioned to continue Ian Hikel's petition to October 1, 2026 at 7pm

2nd: D. Petrelli

Vote by Roll Call: C. Matera, Aye; D. Petrelli, Aye; R. Deschenes, Aye; Z. Foley, Aye

Motion passed

### 7:49pm- D. Petrelli motioned to adjourn

2nd: C. Matera

Vote by Roll Call: K. Bergeson, Aye; D. Petrelli, Aye; Zack Foley, Aye

Motion passed
